As fall approaches, many homeowners begin preparing their homes for the months ahead. Whether you’re organizing seasonal decorations or tackling overdue cleaning projects, it’s a great time to take a look at the items around your home.


A good place to start is by decluttering. Taking inventory of the items around your home can help free up space, improve organization, and reduce unnecessary waste. Before throwing things away, consider whether they can be donated, reused, or recycled instead.


**Why Fall is a Great Time to Declutter**


While spring cleaning often gets the spotlight, fall can be just as valuable for home organization. As routines change and the weather cools, many families begin spending more time indoors, preparing their homes for upcoming holiday gatherings and seasonal activities.


Decluttering can help you:


- Create additional storage space
- Organize seasonal items before they’re needed
- Identify items that can be donated before the holidays
- Make room for new purchases and gifts
- Reduce unnecessary waste
- Start the season with a more organized home


Even tackling one area at a time will make your home feel more manageable heading into fall.


**Start with Areas that Collect the Most Clutter**


Decluttering an entire home can feel overwhelming, so focus on one area at a time.


Consider focusing on areas such as:


- Entryway closets
- Kitchen cabinets and pantries
- Home offices
- Garages and storage rooms
- Children’s bedrooms and playrooms


As you sort through belongings, ask yourself a few questions:


- Have I used this in the past year?
- Do I have more than one?
- Is it still in good condition?
- Could someone else benefit from it?


Your answers will help determine whether an item should be kept, donated, recycled, or discarded.


**Donate Items that Still Have Value**


Many items no longer serving a purpose in your home may still be useful to someone else. Depending on local donation guidelines, organizations often accept clothing, shoes, books, toys, games, kitchenware, blankets and linens, and other household items. Donating gently used items can help reduce landfill waste while giving others in your community access to resources they may need.


**Don’t Forget About Old Electronics**


Old phones, chargers, tablets, computers, and other electronics often end up tucked away in drawers or storage bins. Rather than throwing them away, look for local electronics recycling programs or community collection events. Proper recycling can recover valuable materials while keeping unnecessary waste out of landfills. If you’re replacing older electronics or appliances, this may also be an opportunity to explore newer, energy-efficient options like ENERGY STAR® certified products.


**Look for Opportunities to Reuse**


Not every item needs to be donated or recycled. Sometimes a new purpose is all it takes to extend an item’s life.


For example:


- Glass jars can be reused for pantry or storage organization.
- Old T-shirts can become cleaning cloths.
- Storage bins can be repurposed for seasonal decorations.
- Furniture may be refinished instead of replaced.


Finding new uses for existing items can help reduce waste while providing more value from everyday household products.


**Make Future Purchases More Intentional**


One of the benefits of decluttering is gaining a better understanding of what you already have. As you organize your home, consider whether future purchases are likely to provide long-term value. Prioritizing quality, durability, and reusability can help prevent excess clutter and minimize waste over time. Properly maintaining household items, utilizing reusable containers, and purchasing only what you need will help you make the most of your home’s resources.


**A Fresh Start for the Season Ahead**


As you prepare your home for a new season, donating and recycling unwanted items can help reduce waste, support your community, and create more organized living spaces.
